subject.title: fix: order ambient transcript watermarks by decimal ids

question: What durable same-timestamp watermark contract should OpenClaw use when a channel supplies opaque IDs that cannot be ordered with canonical decimal IDs?
rationale: A scalar lexical order is deterministic but invents a channel order and can discard unseen messages; source ordering and persistence shape determine the correct repair boundary.

options.title: Represent opaque IDs without cross-format ordering
options.body: Use a source ordering key when the channel has one, or retain seen IDs at the latest timestamp so an unseen mixed-format ID is never suppressed.

options.title: Restrict watermarks to ordered channel IDs
options.body: Document and enforce that ambient transcript watermark producers must provide canonical ordered IDs, routing opaque-ID channels through a channel-specific adapter.

options.title: Accept lexical ordering
options.body: Keep the proposed total lexical fallback and explicitly accept that mixed-format same-timestamp IDs may not reflect delivery order.

recommendation.title: Represent opaque IDs without cross-format ordering
recommendation.body: Use a source ordering key when the channel has one, or retain seen IDs at the latest timestamp so an unseen mixed-format ID is never suppressed.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only concrete routing candidate identified in the supplied PR activity for this watermark discussion.
